headerDisplay:
Exposes a ProGrade / DTston grill thermometer to HomeKit. The device reports straight to this machine over UDP — no vendor app, no cloud account, no extra hardware.

Point the device here first with `dplus/lsd_wifi.py configure --host <device-ip> --server <this machine> --server-port 17000 --yes`.
footerDisplay: The field mapping below is already correct for the ProGrade EM2251: the probe temperature is the little-endian pair at body offsets 5-6, in tenths of a degree Celsius. A different unit may differ - recover it with `dplus/udp_listen.py` then `dplus/analyze.py`.

transport.title: Transport

oneOf.title: UDP — the device reports to us (normal)
Simulator — test HomeKit with no hardware

transport.description: Leave as UDP unless you are testing without hardware. The simulator reports fabricated temperatures.

listenPort.title: UDP listen port
listenPort.description: Must match the port set on the device with AT+NETP. The stock firmware uses 17000.

bindAddress.title: Bind address
bindAddress.description: Leave as 0.0.0.0 to listen on all interfaces.

pollSeconds.title: Status poll interval (seconds)
pollSeconds.description: 0 means passive: the device reports on its own, about once a second. Only set this if yours stays silent until asked.

staleSeconds.title: Treat readings as stale after (seconds)
staleSeconds.description: After this long with no frame, HomeKit is told the sensor is inactive rather than left showing an old temperature.

staticTargetC.title: Target temperature, in Celsius
staticTargetC.description: The thermometer does not transmit its own alarm setpoint, so set it here and the plugin publishes a Target sensor plus a Target Reached contact sensor you can build a notification automation on. 225 F = 107.2, 203 F = 95, 165 F = 73.9. Leave blank for no target.

exposeTarget.title: Expose the target temperature as a second sensor
exposeTarget.description: Only appears if a target is available, either from the device or from the setting above.

exposeAlarm.title: Expose "target reached" as a contact sensor
exposeAlarm.description: Contact Detected means the probe has reached the target — useful as an automation trigger for a notification.

exposeBattery.title: Expose the battery level
exposeBattery.description: Only appears if the device actually reports a battery level. The EM2251 does not.

probe.title: Probe temperature field
probe.description: Offset notation from analyze.py: b4 (one byte), be4:5 (big-endian pair), le4:5 (little-endian pair). le5:6 is correct for the ProGrade EM2251.

target.title: Target temperature field
target.description: Blank on the EM2251, which does not transmit its setpoint. Use the target setting above instead.

alarm.title: Alarm / target-reached flag field
alarm.description: Leave blank to derive it by comparing probe against target.

battery.title: Battery percent field
battery.description: Blank on the EM2251, which does not report a battery level. Leave empty and no battery tile is published.

scale.title: Scale (a in temp = a*raw + b)
scale.description: 1 = whole degrees, 0.1 = tenths. 0.1 is correct for the ProGrade EM2251.

unit.title: Unit the device reports in
unit.description: HomeKit always stores Celsius; the Home app displays whichever unit your iPhone is set to.

acknowledge.title: Acknowledge the device's messages
acknowledge.description: Echoes each datagram back to the thermometer. Required: it will not send a temperature unless its heartbeat is acknowledged. Only turn this off for diagnostics.
